identity.node_shape: Rounded dark rectangle with a coloured title bar — blue for function calls, red for events, grey for flow control, purple for function entry/return.
identity.port_style: Named pins stud both walls: white triangles for exec, coloured circles for data; hollow when unwired, solid when wired; a diamond means by-reference.
identity.wire_style: Bezier arrows. White means execution order; every other colour is a data TYPE (red bool, green float, blue object, magenta string).
identity.one_line: Two wire systems share one canvas — a white execution wire says WHEN a node runs, coloured typed wires say WHAT flows, and they never mix.

constructs.mark: Inside: a purple-headed entry node titled with the function name, exec output plus its parameters as right-side data pins; a matching purple ReturnNode closes it.
constructs.quote: Functions have a single entry point designated by a node with the name of the Function

constructs.mark: Named pins on both walls: white triangles for exec, coloured circles for data. Outline when unwired, solid when wired. Colour is the type, never the role.
constructs.named_thing: Pin — Execution Pins and Data Pins
constructs.quote: Pins on the left are input pins, while those on the right of the node are outputs.

constructs.mark: Blue title bar with a ƒ glyph over an italic "Target is <Class>" subtitle; one exec triangle in, one out, Target and argument pins left, return right.
constructs.quote: Function Call nodes always have only a single input execution pin and a single output execution pin

constructs.mark: A grey-blue SET node sitting ON the white exec line, the variable's name as its input pin; reading it back elsewhere is a rounded pill-shaped Get node.
constructs.named_thing: Set node (Setter) / Get node (Getter); Promote to Variable
constructs.quote: Set nodes enable you to change the value of a variable.

constructs.mark: No node at all — an unwired input pin grows an editable widget on the node body itself: X/Y/Z number boxes, a checkbox, an enum dropdown, a "self" box.
A compact GREEN-headed node (Is Simulating Physics, Append, +) carrying only coloured data pins and no white triangles at all; it hangs off to the side of the exec line.
constructs.quote: Pure Functions are wired to Data Pins and are automatically executed by the compiler when the data

constructs.mark: Grey-headed "Branch": one exec triangle in, a red Condition dot below it, two exec triangles out labelled True and False. A Switch stacks one exec exit per case plus Default.
constructs.named_thing: Branch; Switch on Int / String / Name / Enum
constructs.quote: The Branch node serves as a simple way to create decision-based flow from a single true/false condition.

constructs.mark: A small exec-less node: wildcard Option 0, Option 1 … pins stacked in, an Index pin beneath them, one value pin out. "Add pin" grows the option list.
constructs.quote: Return the option at Index, (first option is indexed at 0)

constructs.mark: Grey ForLoop node: First Index / Last Index int pins in; right wall stacks Loop Body exec, Index value, Completed exec. The body hangs OUTSIDE — no enclosing frame.
constructs.quote: This outputs an execution pulse on each iteration of the loop as it moves between the indices.

constructs.mark: Same node silhouette as ForLoop, but a red Condition dot replaces the two index pins; outputs are only Loop Body and Completed — no Index value comes out.
constructs.quote: A test condition and a body are all that make up a WhileLoop.

constructs.mark: A fourth exec triangle named Break on the loop node's LEFT wall; the body wires backwards into it — usually through a Custom Event so no wire wraps around.
constructs.quote: A Custom Event is used for visual clarity, to eliminate the need to have the wire wrap back around

constructs.mark: No feedback wire, shift register or carried pin exists — a data wire cannot run backwards into the loop node. You draw Get → operator → SET inside the body instead.
No lambda-carrying node. The author draws ForEachLoop → Branch → Add-to-array, four nodes and a body. "Filter Array" only matches an Actor class, not a predicate.
constructs.quote: Filter an array based on a Class derived from Actor.

constructs.mark: Repetition is drawn on the EXEC side: Loop Body pulses once per element while Array Element / Index re-present a fresh value. No data pin fires on its own.
constructs.named_thing: Loop Body exec output; Event node
constructs.quote: This outputs an execution pulse on each iteration of the loop as it moves between the indices.

constructs.mark: A Cast node grows a SECOND exec output, "Cast Failed", beneath the normal one — failure is just another white wire. No try/except bracket, no finally, no frame.
constructs.named_thing: Cast To <Class> — the Cast Failed exec pin
constructs.quote: We can do so by dragging off the Other pin of the Event Hit and Casting To our MyCharacter Blueprint.

constructs.mark: Nothing brackets a lifetime. Acquire and release are two ordinary nodes sitting on the same white exec line; a grey comment box is the only visible pairing.
The selection becomes one titled node whose pins were auto-made from the wires that crossed the boundary; double-click opens a tab holding Inputs and Outputs tunnel nodes.
constructs.named_thing: Collapsed Graph, Collapse Nodes / Expand Node, Tunnels, Macro
constructs.quote: The Inputs tunnel node acts as the entry point into the collapsed graph.

constructs.mark: A data output fans out to many wires straight off the pin. Exec fan-out needs a Sequence node — Then 0 / Then 1 / "Add pin ✚". There is no join node.
constructs.quote: The Sequence node allows for a single execution pulse to trigger a series of events in order.

constructs.mark: The white arrowed exec wire alone orders two nodes sharing no data; Sequence turns one pulse into Then 0, Then 1, Then 2, fired top-to-bottom with no delay.
constructs.quote: Exec wires are displayed as white arrows spanning from an output exec pin to an input exec pin.

constructs.mark: The receiver arrives on a "Target" pin whose default box reads self, or on a DIAMOND "Struct Ref" pin; Set members in LinearColor re-emits it on Struct Out.
constructs.named_thing: Target pin (self); Set members in <Struct>; Struct Ref
constructs.quote: Except for the Event node, each node has a Target input pin

constructs.mark: The function rides a red hollow SQUARE pin labelled Event — squares mean delegate, circles mean value — wired into a "Bind Event to <Dispatcher>" node.
constructs.named_thing: Event Dispatcher; Bind Event to <name>; Create Event
constructs.quote: The bind, unbind, and assign methods enable you to add events to the Event Dispatcher's event list

constructs.mark: No glyph whatsoever — the function's own blue ƒ call node placed inside its own graph. A Macro cannot do it: macros are inlined, so the compiler refuses.
constructs.quote: Unlike Functions, Macros can have more than one output execution pin

constructs.mark: A second SET node for the same name further along the white exec wire. Nothing greys or crosses out the first — only the wire's direction says which one wins.
constructs.quote: these must be called by an execution wire in order to execute

constructs.mark: "Break MyStruct": blue header, one struct pin in, one coloured pin per member out. Or right-click a pin → Split Struct Pin and sub-pins indent in place, no new node.
constructs.quote: The pure node that Break creates provides one output pin for each property tagged as BlueprintReadOnly or BlueprintReadWrite.

constructs.mark: It looks synchronous: Delay is an ordinary node on the exec line with a Duration pin; async action nodes grow extra exec outputs (Completed, OnFailure) that fire later.
constructs.quote: Perform a latent action with a delay (specified in seconds).

constructs.mark: Types, scope and pure-node evaluation order never appear on canvas; comments are a grey bubble or a resizable coloured box carrying no semantics; unconnected pins can be hidden.
constructs.named_thing: Comment box (press C); Hide Unconnected Pins; My Blueprint / Details panels
constructs.quote: You can add comments into your blueprints to create visual-only notes that group nodes together

identity.node_shape: A dark rounded rectangle with a header bar carrying the node's name, a type icon and any dropdown controls; ports stack down both side walls.
identity.port_style: Named labels beside the pin; inputs left, outputs right. Control ports draw an arrow icon, data ports a type-coloured icon matching their type.
identity.wire_style: Curved edges. Control edges are always white; data edges are coloured by the type they carry, green for any type without a colour pellet.
identity.one_line: A Script Graph is a left-to-right board of dark node blocks stitched by a white control wire that says what runs next and type-coloured data wires that say what values flow — and every branch, loop, try/catch and subgraph is a single node whose right wall sprays several white arrow ports, never an enclosing frame or region.

constructs.mark: A Subgraph node: one collapsed block titled with the graph's name, arrow control ports and type-coloured data ports on its walls. By default it has no ports.
constructs.named_thing: Subgraph (a Script Graph asset) / Subgraph node
constructs.quote: A Subgraph appears as a single node inside a parent Script Graph.

constructs.mark: A labelled pin on the node's left (input) or right (output) wall; an arrow icon for control, a type-coloured icon for data, names set in the Graph Inspector.
constructs.named_thing: Control Port / Data Port; on a Subgraph: Trigger Input, Trigger Output, Data Input, Data Output
constructs.quote: An input port or output port can be a Control Port or a Data Port

constructs.mark: A Subgraph node wired in by its white Trigger Input arrow — the call site is the node itself; no separate call glyph, no argument list, just its data ports.
constructs.named_thing: Subgraph node (static, wired) / Trigger Custom Event node (dynamic, by name)
constructs.quote: Use a Subgraph node to reference and trigger another Script Graph's logic from inside a parent Script Graph.

constructs.mark: A Set Variable node on the white control wire: scope dropdown in the header, a typed Name field, one data input. Get Variable reads it back by name.
constructs.named_thing: Set Variable / Get Variable node; Flow variable; the Blackboard
constructs.quote: You can't create a Flow variable from the Blackboard - you can create one with a Set Variable node

constructs.mark: A small Literal node — a single value field and one coloured data output, no control ports — or no node at all: an inline value field drawn beside the port.
constructs.named_thing: Float Literal / Integer Literal nodes; Inline Value
constructs.quote: An inline value appears as an object picker field next to a port.

constructs.mark: A compact node titled by the operation (Add, Less, Greater) with A and B coloured data inputs left, one output right, and no white control wire touching it.
constructs.named_thing: Add / Less / Greater nodes (Math, Logic categories); node overloads; Formula node
constructs.quote: For example, to get the result of A + B with the Add node

constructs.mark: An If node: white arrow in plus a Condition data port left; two white arrow outputs stacked right, True above False. Switch grows one arrow per case plus Default.
constructs.named_thing: If node; Switch node (Switch On Enum / String / Integer); the Default port
constructs.quote: Branching nodes split the control flow based on a value.

constructs.mark: A Select node: a selector data port and one coloured data input per option on the left, a single data output right. No white control wire touches it.
constructs.named_thing: Select node (Select On Integer / Enum / String); Toggle Value node; Null Coalesce
constructs.quote: You can select a single value from a set of options based on a selector.

constructs.mark: A For Loop node with First/Last/Step data inputs; its right wall stacks a white Body arrow above a white Exit arrow, plus an Index output. No enclosing frame.
constructs.named_thing: For Loop; For Each Loop; Body port; Exit port; Index / Item outputs; Dictionary checkbox
constructs.quote: For is a numeric loop and requires three integers: a start index, an end index, and a step.

constructs.mark: A While Loop node: Condition data input left; white Body and Exit arrows stacked right. The body is a wire off Body, run to completion inside one frame.
constructs.quote: The while loop is the simplest form of loop. It repeats its body while its condition remains true.

constructs.mark: A Break Loop node — a stub block with one white arrow in and none out, ending a body branch; entering it fires the enclosing loop's Exit arrow.
constructs.named_thing: Break Loop node (no Continue node; no early-return node — an Output node is the only exit)
constructs.quote: As soon as this node is entered, the exit port of the loop is called

constructs.mark: Nothing. No feedback edge and no loop-carried port — a data wire back into the loop would be a cycle. Authors draw a Set/Get Variable pair inside the body.
constructs.quote: Flow variables are like local variables in a scripting language: they have the smallest scope.

constructs.mark: Nothing. No map or filter node and no collection-shaped wire. Authors draw a For Each Loop with a Set Variable accumulator, or type the expression into a Formula node.
constructs.quote: Formula is a powerful node that evaluates logical and mathematical expressions directly via a textual Formula

constructs.mark: Closest is a loop's white Body arrow, which fires once per iteration down the same branch. No generator node, no multi-valued wire, no repeating data port.
constructs.named_thing: Body port on For Loop / For Each Loop / While Loop; green Event nodes re-enter the graph
constructs.quote: The logic to be repeated is called the body of the loop.

constructs.mark: A Try Catch node: one white arrow in, three white arrows stacked right — Try, Catch, Finally — with an Exception data output beside Catch. Throw is a separate block.
constructs.named_thing: Try Catch node (Try / Catch / Finally ports, Exception output); Throw node; Null Check
constructs.quote: The Finally branch is optional. It is always called after Try or Catch

constructs.mark: No with-block, no region frame. The only scoped-cleanup mark is the third white arrow on Try Catch, labelled Finally; the disposal branch hangs off it.
constructs.named_thing: Finally port on the Try Catch node
constructs.quote: It is usually used to dispose or destroy any resources that must be freed.

constructs.mark: One Subgraph node; inside the child, a single Input node with outputs only and a single Output node with inputs only mirror its wall ports. Edit Graph drills in.
constructs.named_thing: Subgraph node; Input node; Output node; State Unit; Embed vs Graph source
constructs.quote: You can only use a single Input node and a single Output node in a Script Graph.

constructs.mark: One data output sprays many coloured edges freely. A control output may not — one white arrow goes to one arrow in; many white arrows may converge on one input.
constructs.named_thing: Multiple Connections; Sequence node (for control fan-out); Wait For Script node (join)
constructs.quote: You can connect a single Data Output port to multiple Data Input ports.

constructs.mark: A Sequence node: one white arrow in, a numbered stack of white arrow outputs 0,1,2… on the right wall fired top-down; the count is a field in its header.
constructs.quote: You can use the special Sequence node under Control for this purpose.

constructs.mark: An action node like Transform Set Position: white arrow in above a Target data port defaulting to Self, white arrow out right. The receiver enters as a port.
constructs.named_thing: Transform Set Position / Transform Rotate / Set Variable; the Target port; the This node
constructs.quote: A node can listen for events, get the value of a variable, modify a component on a GameObject

constructs.mark: Nothing — no wire carries a function. Instead a Trigger Custom Event node holds the target object and the event name typed as a string; the link is drawn nowhere.
constructs.quote: Enter the name of the event exactly as it is sensitive to case and whitespace.

constructs.mark: Undrawable — the editor refuses to let a Subgraph node point at its own graph file, so no node calls itself. Authors re-enter via a named Trigger Custom Event.
constructs.quote: You can't nest a Script Graph as a Subgraph in its own graph file.

constructs.mark: A second Set Variable node further along the white wire carrying the same Name string. The two nodes never touch; nothing on the board marks the shadowing.
constructs.named_thing: Set Variable node (same Name, same Scope)
constructs.quote: you can give a node the name of a variable, instead of a fixed value or text

constructs.mark: Usually one getter node per field — Vector 3 Get X, Get Y, Get Z — each fed the same coloured wire. An Expose node fans every member out at once.
constructs.named_thing: Vector 3 Get X / Get Y / Get Z nodes; Expose node
constructs.quote: Exposes all members of the type.

constructs.mark: A Coroutine checkbox puts a small dual-arrow icon on the green event node's header; Wait For Seconds / Wait Until then sit inline on the white control wire.
constructs.named_thing: Coroutine checkbox; Wait For Seconds / Wait Until / Wait While / Wait For End Of Frame / Wait For Script; Cooldown; Timer
constructs.quote: A small dual-arrow icon appears on the event, indicating that it runs as a coroutine.

constructs.mark: Expressions, types and names: a Formula node hides a whole expression in one text field; Switch cases, Subgraph ports and variables are authored in Inspector and Blackboard panels.
constructs.named_thing: Graph Inspector; the Blackboard; Formula node; fuzzy finder; node groups (colour box, cosmetic only)
constructs.quote: Nodes display the required information as text, but editing is done via the Inspector.

identity.node_shape: A small square icon - a primitive glyph or a subVI's hand-drawn picture - with short wire stubs on its left (inputs) and right (outputs) edges.
identity.port_style: Unnamed stubs on the icon's edge, addressed by connector-pane POSITION; hover the wiring tool to see the name and a highlighted terminal.
identity.wire_style: Thin orthogonal polyline, no arrowheads. Colour, thickness and pattern ARE the type: orange DBL, blue I32, dotted green Boolean, pink string, dash-hatched olive error.
identity.one_line: A LabVIEW diagram is a wired circuit board where a node fires the instant every required input has data - so the only way to order two things is to run a wire between them, and where no real data flows, the dark-yellow error cluster wire is the wire you invent.

constructs.mark: A subVI node: a small square hand-drawn picture icon with short wire stubs on its edges. Its interface is the Connector Pane, a grid of rectangles beside the VI Icon.
constructs.named_thing: VI / subVI (interface = Connector Pane, drawn by the VI Icon)
constructs.quote: SubVIs are VIs that are called from another VI.

constructs.mark: A rectangle in the connector-pane grid (4x2x2x4 default), addressed by POSITION not name. Inputs left, outputs right, error in/out in the bottom corners. Required shows bold in Context Help.
constructs.named_thing: Connector pane terminal; Required / Recommended / Optional
constructs.quote: Put inputs on the left side of the Connector Pane and outputs on the right.

constructs.mark: Drop the VI's icon onto another diagram and wire it. Identical in shape to a primitive - no call glyph, no frame; only the icon art distinguishes yours from the + triangle.
constructs.named_thing: subVI call (drop the VI Icon on the Block Diagram)
constructs.quote: Dropping that VI on a Block Diagram of another VI

constructs.mark: Nothing. The wire IS the value and is anonymous. A free label on it is a comment. The escape hatch is a Local Variable: a small box printing a front-panel control's name.
constructs.named_thing: (none) - free label, or Local Variable node
constructs.quote: Using Local Variables breaks data flow execution.

constructs.mark: A Constant: a small boxed value sitting loose on the diagram with an output stub only, no input. Border colour is the type - blue 10, orange 0.5, green T/F.
constructs.named_thing: Constant (Numeric Constant, Boolean Constant, String Constant, Enum Constant)
constructs.quote: A source can be a Control Terminal, Constant, or the output from a Node.

constructs.mark: A tiny cream/yellow triangle pointing right with the symbol inside (+, x, >=). Wire stubs land on the flat left edge; the point on the right is the single output.
constructs.named_thing: primitive function (Functions palette: Numeric, Comparison, Boolean)
constructs.quote: Performs a built-in operation. The small icon is the operator; wires land on typed terminals around its edge.

constructs.mark: Case Structure: a hatched grey frame, selector label with left/right arrows and a dropdown centred on top, a green ? selector terminal on the left inner wall. Only one case visible, others stacked behind.
constructs.named_thing: Case Structure (case selector label, selector terminal, Subdiagram, Default case)
constructs.quote: can have multiple Subdiagrams (also known as "Cases"), one of which is selectively executed at runtime

constructs.mark: Select function: a black right-pointing triangle with a ? inside; three stubs on its flat left edge - t top, s middle, f bottom - and one output at the point.
constructs.quote: The Select function returns the value wired to the t input or f input, depending on the value of s.

constructs.mark: For Loop: grey frame with a folded dog-ear bottom-right corner, a blue N count terminal top-left and blue i iteration terminal bottom-left. An array in through a [ ] indexing tunnel makes it for-each.
constructs.named_thing: For Loop (count terminal N, iteration terminal i, auto-indexing tunnel)
constructs.quote: determined by the numeric value written to the "N" terminal of the loop, or by the size of an array

constructs.mark: While Loop: a thick grey rounded-corner frame with a blue i iteration terminal bottom-left and a red stop-sign octagon (Stop if True) as conditional terminal bottom-right.
constructs.named_thing: While Loop (conditional terminal; Stop if True / Continue if True)
constructs.quote: A While Loop is a primitive structure that repeats the code within its subdiagram until a Boolean condition is met.

constructs.mark: No break, continue or return glyph exists. A Boolean wired TRUE to the conditional terminal ends the loop AFTER this iteration finishes. Early return is a Case Structure wrapping the remaining work.
constructs.named_thing: conditional terminal (For Loop, added LabVIEW 8.5); Stop on Error
constructs.quote: This conditional terminal is useful if a condition has been met that would make further iterations of the loop unnecessary.

constructs.mark: Shift register: a matched pair of small squares on the loop's left and right walls, the left carrying a down-arrow and the right an up-arrow. Stack more left terminals for i-2, i-3.
constructs.named_thing: Shift Register (left/right terminals, stacked shift register); Feedback Node
constructs.quote: pass data from one iteration of the loop to the next iteration of the loop

constructs.mark: Polymorphic primitives auto-map: an array wire into the + triangle is elementwise with no loop drawn. Filter is a Conditional output tunnel - a ? square on the wall with a Boolean stub under it.
constructs.named_thing: polymorphic function on an array wire; Conditional (indexing) tunnel
constructs.quote: the tunnel will output a 1D array containing all loop iteration values where a TRUE was wired

constructs.mark: Channel Wire: a thick orange double-outlined tube between a writer node and a reader node, crossing loop walls. A plain port never fires twice - one node execution, one value.
constructs.named_thing: Channel Wire (Stream / Tag / Message channel); Queue refnum
constructs.quote: Stream Channels: Allow for continuous data streaming from producer to consumer.

constructs.mark: The error cluster wire: dark yellow with a black dash-hatch inside it, entering each node's bottom-left and leaving bottom-right. Catch is a Case Structure with a green No Error frame and a red Error frame.
constructs.named_thing: error cluster (status / code / source), error in, error out, Error Case Structure, Merge Errors, Automatic Error Handling
constructs.quote: The border of the error case is red and the non-error case is green.

constructs.mark: No with-frame. An Open - Use - Close chain of subVI icons strung on one refnum wire plus the error wire. The In Place Element structure IS a frame, pairing in/out border nodes.
constructs.named_thing: refnum Open/Close chain; In Place Element Structure border nodes
constructs.quote: Use the In Place Element structure when you operate on a data element within an array, cluster, variant, or waveform

constructs.mark: Select nodes, then Edit - Create SubVI: the selection collapses into one square icon with a generated connector pane. Double-click it and its own block diagram opens in a new window.
constructs.named_thing: Create SubVI; Subdiagram (for the in-place structure frames)
constructs.quote: There is no difference between a VI and a SubVI except the relationship in Calling Heirarchy.

constructs.mark: Fan-out: the wire forks at a small solid dot and every branch gets the same value. There is no join node - a Case Structure's single output tunnel square on the right wall is the merge.
constructs.named_thing: wire branch / junction; output tunnel; Use Default If Unwired; Linked Input Tunnel
constructs.quote: A wire can be forked to input the same data into two or more different sinks.

constructs.mark: Flat Sequence Structure: frames side by side inside a film-strip border of sprocket holes, running left to right. Idiomatically replaced by threading the error wire through both nodes instead.
constructs.named_thing: Flat Sequence Structure (Frame); Stacked Sequence Structure; error wire chaining
constructs.quote: Use error in (no error) and error out terminals instead of flat sequence structures to enforce sequential execution of VIs.

constructs.mark: No receiver to mutate - wires carry copies. In Place Element structure: a frame whose left border node splits an element out and whose right border node puts it back in the same memory.
constructs.named_thing: In Place Element Structure; Data Value Reference; Property Node (write arrow)
constructs.quote: without requiring the LabVIEW compiler to copy data values and maintain those values in memory

constructs.mark: A strictly-typed VI Reference rides a wire into a Call By Reference Node, which draws the target's connector pane on its own face with the refnum stub on its top-left.
constructs.named_thing: strictly typed VI Reference; Call By Reference Node; Static VI Reference
constructs.quote: You can wire to these terminals just as you would to a normal subVI.

constructs.mark: Drop the VI's own icon inside its own block diagram, inside a Case Structure. Nothing on the diagram marks it - reentrancy is an invisible VI Properties radio button.
constructs.named_thing: recursive VI; Shared clone reentrant execution
constructs.quote: a VI that can calls itself as a SubVI where the SubVI call is in a Case Structure

constructs.mark: Nothing. A wire has exactly one source forever and cannot be re-pointed. The nearest drawing is a shift register terminal overwriting last iteration's value at the loop wall.
constructs.quote: The wire has a defined data type determined by the source

constructs.mark: Unbundle By Name: a pale-yellow node whose rows print the field NAMES, each in that field's own wire colour. Plain Unbundle prints only type glyphs in cluster order.
constructs.named_thing: Unbundle By Name / Unbundle; Bundle By Name for the inverse
constructs.quote: The Unbundle by Name function returns the cluster elements whose names you specify.

constructs.mark: Two loop frames simply sit side by side with no wire between them - the physical separation IS the concurrency. No await glyph; a blocking Dequeue or channel reader node is the wait.
constructs.named_thing: parallel loops; Queue / Channel Wire; Asynchronous Call By Reference; Event Structure
constructs.quote: designed to transfer data across different execution contexts, such as between loops running in parallel

constructs.mark: Invisible by design: execution order (no exec wire), type annotations (the wire colour IS the type), reentrancy/priority/inlining (VI Properties radio buttons), and every case but the visible one.
constructs.named_thing: VI Properties; the wire's own colour and thickness
constructs.quote: Under Reentrancy radio buttons, select the Shared clone reentrant execution

identity.flow: left-to-right for data; control and action signals enter from the top edge of the box they fire
identity.node_shape: A white or gradient-filled rectangle whose icon IS the operation - a formula, waveform, triangle or z-1 glyph - with its name lettered below the box.
identity.port_style: Small solid arrowhead stubs on the left and right walls, numbered 1..n or lettered (u1, N, cond, Y0); Inport/Outport are separate capsule blocks.
identity.wire_style: Thin black arrow = data signal; dot-dashed with a downward arrowhead or filled ball = action/function-call control; hollow triple tram-line = a named bus.
identity.one_line: A left-to-right signal-flow schematic where rectangles compute and thin black arrows carry a value that exists at every time step, with a separate dot-dashed control line whose only job is to say WHEN a boxed region runs.

constructs.mark: Thin-bordered rectangle groups blocks for looks; thick-bordered rectangle is atomic. Name lettered below the box; numbered port stubs on left and right walls.
constructs.quote: A block that represents a virtual subsystem has a thin border.

constructs.mark: Rounded-end capsule holding a number, placed inside the subsystem; it materialises as a numbered stub on the parent rectangle's left or right wall.
constructs.named_thing: Inport / Outport (In Bus Element / Out Bus Element)
constructs.quote: The ports on a Subsystem block correspond to blocks inside the subsystem.

constructs.mark: Rectangle lettered 'caller / timestwo()' with named pins x and y; a thin line from its top ends in a filled black ball on the callee.
constructs.named_thing: Function Caller + Simulink Function / Function-Call Subsystem
constructs.quote: Function-Call Subsystem — Subsystem whose execution is controlled by external function-call input

constructs.mark: No binding node. The name is lettered under the arrow itself; matching bracketed Goto/From tag blocks continue that named signal with no line drawn between them.
constructs.named_thing: Signal name / signal label propagation; Goto and From tags
constructs.quote: The Subsystem block supports signal label propagation through subsystem Inport and Outport blocks.

constructs.mark: Plain rectangle whose entire icon is the value - 0.5, 10, [0 0 0] - with no stub on its left wall and one arrow leaving the right.
Shape-coded primitives: Gain is a triangle with its factor inside, Sum a circle with +/- beside each input stub, comparison a rectangle lettered <=.
constructs.named_thing: Gain, Sum, Product, Relational Operator, Logical Operator blocks

constructs.mark: If rectangle's right wall carries text ports if(u1>0), elseif(u2>0), else; from each a dot-dashed line drops into its own subsystem's top edge.
constructs.named_thing: If block + If Action Subsystem (Action Port); Switch Case block
constructs.quote: The dot-dashed lines from the 'If' block denote control signals

constructs.mark: Tall narrow rectangle with three left stubs (data, control, data) and a diagonal lever line drawn inside, pointing at whichever input is currently passed through.
constructs.quote: The Switch block passes through the first input or the third input

constructs.mark: A small 'For Iterator' rectangle sits inside the subsystem; an optional left stub N takes the count, a right stub lettered 1:N emits the current index.
constructs.named_thing: For Iterator block / For Iterator Subsystem
constructs.quote: the block diagram equivalent of a for loop in a programming language

constructs.mark: A 'While Iterator' rectangle inside the subsystem with left stubs lettered cond and IC; the condition is computed by blocks drawn inside that same frame.
constructs.named_thing: While Iterator block / While Iterator Subsystem
constructs.quote: the block diagram equivalent of a while loop in a programming language

constructs.mark: Nothing drawn. The only exit is the cond stub, recomputed inside the frame each pass; the ceiling is a number typed into the block's dialog.
constructs.quote: Specify maximum number of iterations allowed during a time step.

constructs.mark: Small square whose whole icon is 1/z (or a step glyph, Memory), wired from a Sum's output back around to its own input as a visible closed ring.
constructs.quote: When placed in an iterator subsystem, it holds and delays its input by one iteration.

constructs.mark: One subsystem rectangle; the whole array enters on an ordinary arrow and is sliced per element inside. No loop, no index, no iterator block is drawn.
constructs.quote: Apply algorithm to individual elements or subarrays of input signals or mask parameters

constructs.mark: No yield glyph - every wire already carries a value each time step. A rate change shows as a coloured or annotated line plus a Rate Transition rectangle.
constructs.named_thing: Sample time colours / Rate Transition; Function-Call Generator
constructs.quote: Use the Rate Transition block instead.

constructs.mark: Nothing on the canvas. The run stops, the Diagnostic Viewer window lists it and highlights the offending block; the handler is a function name typed into a dialog.
constructs.named_thing: Name of error callback function (ErrorFcn); Diagnostic Viewer
constructs.quote: Enter the name of a function to be called if an error occurs

constructs.mark: Nothing. Nearest mark is a reinit stub on the subsystem's top wall fed by a function-call line - a state reset you must fire, not an automatic teardown.
constructs.quote: A reinitialize event port provides a function-call control signal that triggers a subsystem reinitialize event

constructs.mark: Double-click the rectangle and the canvas is replaced by its contents, a Back button appearing under the toolbar; thin border virtual, thick border atomic.
constructs.quote: To view or edit the contents of a subsystem, double-click the Subsystem block.

constructs.mark: Fanout is a filled black dot where one arrow splits. Rejoin is a tall narrow rectangle lettered 'merge' collecting mutually exclusive conditional writers into one arrow.
constructs.named_thing: Signal branch (junction dot) / Merge block / Bus Creator

constructs.mark: No order wire. Grey ordinal numerals sit in each parallel Stateflow state's top-right corner, or separate dot-dashed E1()/E2()/E3() function-call lines are fired in turn.
constructs.named_thing: Parallel state execution order; Function-Call Split; atomic subsystem
constructs.quote: The blocks in a nonvirtual subsystem execute consecutively.

constructs.mark: Assignment rectangle with named stubs Y0, U, Idx1; Bus Assignment shows rows lettered 'Bus' and ':= a'. The whole updated value still leaves on a visible wire.
constructs.named_thing: Assignment / Bus Assignment / Data Store Write

constructs.mark: No function ever rides a data arrow. The callee is lettered as text inside the caller rectangle; only the right to execute travels, on a dot-dashed line.
constructs.quote: Subsystem whose execution is controlled by external function-call input

constructs.mark: No self-call glyph. A rectangle cannot contain itself; feedback with no delay is flagged as an algebraic loop, so the unroll is a For Iterator instead.
constructs.named_thing: algebraic loop (a diagnostic, not a construct)
constructs.quote: Minimize artificial algebraic loop occurrences

constructs.mark: A wire has one source forever. The only repeat-write mark is a Data Store Write rectangle with no output arrow at all, tied to its readers by name.
constructs.named_thing: Data Store Memory / Data Store Write

constructs.mark: Thick solid black vertical bar; the bus enters as a hollow triple tram-line and leaves as separate thin arrows, each lettered with <elementname> in angle brackets.
Dot-dashed line lettered E3() driven by an Asynchronous Interrupt rectangle, landing on the subsystem's top-edge arrow; the scheduler is a rounded cream frame with a trigger glyph.
constructs.named_thing: Asynchronous Interrupt / async function-call; Stateflow scheduler chart

constructs.mark: Numbers live in dialogs, not on the board: iteration limit, initial condition, sample time and error-callback name are all invisible until you open the block.
constructs.quote: You specify the block output for the first sampling period with the Initial conditions parameter.

identity.node_shape: A wide flat horizontal bar: type icon centred, small square flag chips at both the left and right ends, the node's name in text floating beside the bar, not inside it.
identity.port_style: Small unlabelled nubs on the bar's top edge (inputs) and bottom edge (outputs), drawn as triangular tabs or round dots depending on zoom. Addressed positionally, numbered from 0.
identity.wire_style: A thin grey curve with one small arrowhead near its midpoint. One kind only: it means cook dependency. No colour coding, no type, and it carries the whole geometry.
identity.one_line: A top-down chain of flat grey bars carrying one geometry stream, where every branch, count, condition and loop exit is a coloured blob, a lit flag chip, or text typed into an off-canvas parameter field — never a second wire.

constructs.mark: A Subnetwork/HDA node drawn identically to any other bar: one flat bar, type icon, up to four input nubs on the top edge, one output nub below. Double-click to dive in.
constructs.quote: The Subnet op is essentially a way of creating a macro to represent a collection of ops

constructs.mark: Unlabelled nubs on the bar's top edge (inputs) and bottom edge (outputs), addressed by position from 0. Names only surface as a hover tooltip; parameters are off-canvas text fields.
constructs.quote: nodes have input and output connectors, which you connect together with wires

constructs.mark: An Invoke Compiled Block bar with numbered input nubs; the callee is a node PATH typed into its Compile Block field, so no wire ever reaches the definition being called.
constructs.quote: This node runs a compiled block defined elsewhere to process this node’s inputs

constructs.mark: A Null SOP — a pass-through bar sitting in the chain — plus its node name. Object Merge bars elsewhere name that path in a text field; no wire is drawn between them.
constructs.quote: It can act as a fixed place in the network for path references.

constructs.mark: A generator bar with a bare top edge — no input nubs at all (Box, Sphere, Grid). A scalar constant is not a node: it is a number typed in a parameter field.
constructs.quote: Wiring nodes together at the geometry level controls the flow of geometry through the nodes

constructs.mark: No node in SOP networks: `$F >= 5` is text inside a parameter field in the side panel. Only inside a VOP network does arithmetic get its own bar and wires.
constructs.quote: You can control the parameter with an expression or animate it.

constructs.mark: A Switch bar with N input nubs stacked along its top edge and ONE output nub. The chosen index is an expression in Select Input. Branching converges here; it never diverges.
constructs.quote: This node passes the input specified in the Select input parameter to the output.

constructs.mark: The same Switch bar — there is no statement/expression split. Wires pull, so the unselected upstream branch simply never cooks and no second output nub is drawn anywhere.
constructs.quote: lets you choose which upstream branch of a network cooks

constructs.mark: Block Begin and Block End bars wired top-to-bottom, with every node between them wrapped in a rounded tinted blob whose colour is inherited from those two nodes.
constructs.quote: The color of the blob surrounding the nodes in a loop comes from the color

constructs.mark: There is no While node. You draw the ordinary counted blob and type a Stop Condition expression into the Block End's parameter field — invisible on the canvas.
constructs.quote: If this parameter is 1 at the start of an iteration, then looping of the block stops.

constructs.mark: No break pin, no second output nub. The exit is a Stop Condition or Stop Attribute parameter, or a Switch-If bar inside the blob routing to a do-nothing branch.
constructs.quote: Switch away to a branch that sets the Stop Attribute to non-zero and does no other work.

constructs.mark: The blob plus a text badge beside each node reading "(Fetch Feedback : 1)". The carry itself is NOT drawn — no back-edge wire; it is a dropdown plus a Block Path.
constructs.quote: but subsequent iterations use the output of the previous iteration

constructs.mark: One ordinary Attribute Wrangle bar with a Run Over dropdown, or a Copy to Points bar. The per-element iteration has no mark on the canvas at all.
constructs.named_thing: Attribute Wrangle (Run Over) / Copy to Points
constructs.quote: Apply the VEX code to each component of this type (points, primitives/faces, or vertices.

constructs.mark: Not drawn. A SOP wire hands over one whole geometry per cook. Repeated emission belongs to a different network type — TOPs — where nodes fan out work items.
constructs.quote: TOP nodes define a workflow where data is fed into the network, turned into work items

constructs.mark: A red exclamation badge in the row under the node's name — optionally drawn large behind the node — and downstream bars stop cooking. Error SOP is a plain bar that raises one.
constructs.named_thing: Error SOP / error badge / warning badge
constructs.quote: An “error” prevents cooking subsequent nodes, and displays a prominent badge on the node

constructs.mark: No bracket or zone exists. Caching lifetime is a per-node flag chip instead — Lock lit red second-from-left, Unload shown as a badge — and an ordinary cook releases itself.
constructs.quote: Lock “freezes” and caches the node’s output geometry.

constructs.mark: Select bars, Collapse to Subnet, they become one bar. Dive in and four pseudo-node stubs stand in for the subnet's inputs; an Output SOP bar marks the result.
constructs.named_thing: Collapse to Subnet / Dive into Network / Output SOP
constructs.quote: The network view shows four pseudo-nodes which represent the subnet’s inputs.

constructs.mark: One output nub sprouts several wires. Rejoin at a Merge bar whose multi-input grows a fresh nub per wire; an Alt-dragged dot can gather crossing wires into one.
constructs.quote: If you select multiple nodes and connect one of their outputs to a multi-input

constructs.mark: A Null with Copy Input off, wired into a Merge bar purely to force a cook — an ordinary-looking wire carrying nothing. In ROP networks the wire itself means order.
constructs.quote: You can use a Merge SOP to collect dependencies into a single input this way.

constructs.mark: No receiver box and no mutation mark. Every bar in the vertical chain edits the one geometry stream passing through it; the chain itself IS the sequence of edits.
constructs.quote: each node creates or modifies data passing through the node

constructs.mark: Never on a wire. A block is passed as a node path typed into a parameter field with a chooser button — the Compile Block parameter — not as a nub on the bar.
constructs.quote: A path to the last node in the compiled block you want to execute.

constructs.mark: Nothing is drawn. The network is an acyclic top-to-bottom chain and a subnet cannot contain itself; you draw a counted Block Begin/End blob or nest subnets by hand.
constructs.quote: Houdini typically processes the nodes in a geometry network from top to bottom

constructs.mark: Insert a new bar above an existing Null. Every Object Merge naming that Null now reads the new value, and nothing on the canvas is redrawn or re-wired.
constructs.quote: you can add more nodes above the Null without having to change any references to the Null

constructs.mark: Several Output SOP bars inside a subnet, each carrying an output index, give the parent bar extra output nubs. Reading one field is an attribute name typed as text.
constructs.quote: Output index 0 corresponds to the first wire out of the node

constructs.mark: Not drawn in a geometry network: parallelism is a "Multithread when Compiled" checkbox in the parameter pane. Farm-scale concurrency lives in a separate network type, TOPs.
constructs.quote: it may be possible to run each pass on a separate thread

constructs.mark: Every number, condition, iteration count, node path and per-element line of code sits as text in the Parameter Editor beside the canvas. Wires show only which geometry goes where.
constructs.quote: You can control the parameter with an expression or animate it.

identity.node_shape: Rounded dark rectangle: title bar with a collapse chevron on the left, outputs top-right, property widgets in the middle, inputs bottom-left
identity.port_style: Small coloured dots in named rows on the node's left and right edges; colour encodes data type, shape (circle/rectangle/diamond/four-squares/three-lines) encodes data structure
identity.wire_style: Thick smooth bezier noodle taking the colour of the sockets it joins; links through a muted node draw red
identity.one_line: A pull-based dataflow graph where only data is ever wired — control flow is drawn as translucent zone hulls bracketed by paired Input/Output nodes, or as extra input rows on a Switch node.

constructs.mark: A green-titled rounded box. Inside it, a Group Input node at the far left and a Group Output node at the far right carry the named socket rows.
constructs.quote: Group Input and Group Output nodes are used to represent data flowing into and out of the group.

constructs.mark: Little coloured dots in named rows down the node edges — inputs bottom-left, outputs top-right. Colour is the type; shape is the data structure.
constructs.quote: They appear as little colored circles on either side of the node.

constructs.mark: One green-titled box showing only the group's name and its interface sockets, placed via Add ‣ Group; Tab pushes the editor inside it.
constructs.named_thing: Group node (Add ‣ Group, Tab to enter)
constructs.quote: A node group is visually identified by its green title bar.

constructs.mark: No name tag rides a wire. A Capture Attribute or Store Named Attribute node sits in the geometry chain; the name is a text field on the node face.
constructs.named_thing: Capture Attribute Node / Store Named Attribute Node
constructs.quote: stores one or more fields on a geometry, and outputs those same fields

constructs.mark: An unconnected input socket grows an inline widget on the node face — a number field, colour swatch or XYZ triple; or a standalone Value node with one output dot.
constructs.quote: has a default value which can be edited via a color, numeric, or vector interface input

constructs.mark: A small node whose title reads Math, Vector Math, Boolean Math or Compare, with an operation dropdown on its face above two unnamed value input rows.
constructs.named_thing: Math Node / Boolean Math Node / Compare Node / Vector Math Node
constructs.quote: the Math Node node includes functions to convert between degrees and radians

constructs.mark: No branch region and no execution pin. A Switch node with False/True input rows, or an Index Switch stacking rows 0,1,2…; both collapse to ONE output dot.
constructs.named_thing: Switch Node / Index Switch Node / Menu Switch Node
constructs.quote: The Switch node outputs one of two inputs depending on a condition.

constructs.mark: The same Switch node read as an expression: a boolean Switch row, a False row and a True row on the left, one Output dot on the right.
constructs.quote: only the input that is passed through the node is evaluated. This means the unused input is not computed.

constructs.mark: Two nodes both titled Repeat, with a translucent orange hull drawn behind the canvas between them; an Iterations number field sits on the left node.
constructs.named_thing: Repeat Zone / For Each Geometry Element Zone
constructs.quote: an input node on the left, an output node on the right, and an orange area in the middle

constructs.mark: Nothing is drawn. The Repeat Input node carries only an integer Iterations field — no condition socket, no exit pin. Authors over-count and freeze state with an inner Switch.
constructs.quote: Number of times to execute the zone.

constructs.mark: Only on the Simulation zone: a Skip boolean socket on the Simulation Input node that jumps the hull's contents wholesale. Repeat and For Each have no such pin.
constructs.quote: Forward the output of the simulation input node directly to the output node

constructs.mark: Matching named socket rows on both zone nodes: a wire into Repeat Output's row reappears at Repeat Input's same-named row next pass; the orange hull encloses the path.
constructs.quote: These inner nodes can then write to the output node for providing inputs to the next iteration

constructs.mark: A diamond socket. An ordinary node fed a diamond field runs per element with no loop drawn at all; Filter List and Accumulate Field are single boxes over a whole list.
constructs.named_thing: Fields (Diamond) / Filter List Node / Accumulate Field Node
constructs.quote: Represents a value that can vary per element (e.g. per point, edge, or face).

constructs.mark: No socket ever fires twice. A List socket drawn as three stacked horizontal lines hands the entire collection across in one evaluation instead.
constructs.quote: allow multiple values to be passed through a single socket

constructs.mark: A Warning node: a Show boolean row in, a Message text field, a severity dropdown picking the icon, and a Show row passing straight back out. No try/except region exists.
constructs.quote: The warning type also determines the icon used when the message is displayed.

constructs.mark: Nothing. Zone hulls do bracket a region with paired Input/Output nodes and seal it so no wire escapes, but nothing acquires or releases; there is no cleanup mark.
constructs.quote: It is not possible to have any link going towards outside.

constructs.mark: Selected nodes collapse into one green-titled box; Tab pushes the editor inside, where Group Input and Group Output nodes flank the contents. Groups nest.
constructs.quote: Grouping nodes can simplify a node tree by hiding complexity and reusing common functionality.

constructs.mark: One output dot sprouts several bezier wires. Rejoining uses a multi-input socket drawn as an ellipse rather than a circle, stacking many wires into one row.
constructs.named_thing: Multi-input socket (ellipsis shape) / Join Geometry Node
constructs.quote: These sockets will have an ellipsis shape rather than a circle to indicate their special behavior.

constructs.mark: Nothing — no execution wire exists to order anything. Authors thread the Geometry cable serially through both nodes, converting the wanted order into a real data dependency.
constructs.quote: The new attribute is only available in the geometry produced by this node.

constructs.mark: Set Position and Store Named Attribute LOOK like edits — Geometry in on the left, Geometry out on the right — but each emits new geometry; upstream nodes are untouched.
constructs.named_thing: Set Position / Store Named Attribute (value semantics)
constructs.quote: It can’t be read in the geometry of “sibling” or “upstream” nodes.

constructs.mark: A light-brown Closure socket. A Closure zone's output dot wires into the Closure input row of an Evaluate Closure node, whose other rows mirror the closure's signature.
constructs.named_thing: Closure zone / Evaluate Closure Node / Closure socket (light brown)
constructs.quote: It acts as the call site of the closure, running its internal node graph and returning the resulting values.

constructs.mark: Undrawable by construction — a group node cannot be placed inside itself, so no self-edge or back-cable to a group's own box can ever appear on the canvas.
constructs.quote: Recursive node groups are prohibited to avoid infinite recursion.

constructs.mark: An input socket holds one wire only, so dropping a new cable on it visibly deletes the old one. Downstream, a second Store Named Attribute with the same name shadows the first.
constructs.named_thing: Store Named Attribute Node (same name, later in the chain)
constructs.quote: This storing and retrieving of a field can also be done with the Store Named Attribute Node

constructs.mark: A Separate Bundle node: one Bundle input dot on the left, then a stack of named output rows on the right, one per element. Separate XYZ does the same for vectors.
constructs.named_thing: Separate Bundle Node / Separate XYZ Node
constructs.quote: Each output corresponds to an element in the bundle, identified by its socket name.

constructs.mark: Nothing concurrent is drawn. The only time-aware structure is the Simulation zone hull, advanced by the animation frame clock, with a Delta Time socket on its input node.
constructs.quote: It will only be evaluated while the animation frame changes

constructs.mark: Execution order itself. No white control wire, no sequence pin, no start node — the graph is pulled backwards from Group Output, so only data dependency is ever visible.
constructs.quote: Only sockets connected to this node will be available as outputs on the group itself.

identity.node_shape: A grey rounded capsule with its name in white on a dark vertical band down the centre; input grips left wall, output grips right wall.
identity.port_style: Small semicircular grips on the side walls, each labelled with a one- or two-letter abbreviation (L, P, A, B, R); named, never positional.
identity.wire_style: A dark grey bezier from output grip to input grip; single line = one item, double = list, dashed double = tree. Colour carries nothing.
identity.one_line: A pull-based parametric board where every grey capsule recomputes from its lettered grips, and the wire itself draws the shape of the data — single, double or dashed-double — so iteration is read off the cable rather than drawn as a loop.

constructs.mark: A grey rounded capsule, name in white on a dark vertical band down its middle, lettered input grips down the left wall, output grips down the right.
constructs.quote: Components use them to collect existing data and output new data.

constructs.mark: Small semicircular grips notched into the capsule's left and right walls, each carrying a one- or two-letter label (L, P, A, B, R); hover shows the full name.
constructs.quote: The “L” on the right of the “Cull” component is an output parameter.

constructs.mark: No call node and no definition/call-site split: dropping the capsule on the canvas IS the invocation. Reusing a Cluster means placing a second copy of its capsule, wired separately.
constructs.quote: Contains a cluster of Grasshopper components

constructs.mark: No name is ever written. A free-floating capsule (Number Slider, Panel, or a bare parameter) holds the value; downstream reads it only by following the wire out of its grip.
constructs.quote: Parameters can also be used by themselves to store constant data or to redirect data into multiple streams.

constructs.mark: A Number Slider capsule showing a labelled slider track and its value, a yellow Panel rectangle printing the raw text, or data set inside any parameter capsule.
constructs.quote: A lot of parameters in Grasshopper are also capable of storing Persistent Data

constructs.mark: A small capsule whose dark band reads A+B, Larger or Not, with A/B grips in and R (or >, >=) out; or an Expression capsule printing the formula inside its body.
constructs.quote: Evaluate an expression

constructs.mark: A Dispatch capsule: L and P grips in, two output grips A and B. It splits the list, not the execution — both A and B downstream still solve every time.
constructs.quote: Dispatch the items in a list into two target lists.

constructs.mark: A Stream Filter capsule with numbered grips Stream 0, Stream 1 … plus an integer Gate grip G, and one output grip S; the gate index picks which wire's data emerges.
constructs.quote: Filters a collection of input streams

constructs.mark: No loop node, no body outline. The mark is the cable: feed a double-line list wire into an ordinary capsule and it runs once per item, silently.
constructs.quote: the wire connecting a list is drawn as a double line

constructs.mark: Nothing is drawn — no while capsule, no body frame, no back-wire, since the canvas rejects cycles. Authors drop a C#/Python script capsule or a plug-in Loop Start/Loop End pair.
No break mark, no early-return grip, no port that stops anything. The nearest drawing is a Cull Pattern capsule that removes items from the list travelling on the wire.
constructs.quote: Cull (remove) elements in a list using a repeating bit mask.

constructs.mark: No feedback cable exists to draw — wiring an output back upstream is refused. State is faked with a Data Dam capsule plus a Timer, or plug-in loop capsules.
constructs.quote: Delay data on its way through the document

constructs.mark: Every ordinary capsule is the comprehension. Map: push a double-line list into its grip. Filter: a Cull Pattern or Dispatch capsule. Nesting: a tiny StateTag icon on the grip sets Cross Reference.
constructs.named_thing: list matching — Long / Short / Cross Reference
constructs.quote: The Cross Reference matches the first list with each of the elements in the second list

constructs.mark: The word is used everywhere, but a stream is a whole static collection delivered once per solution — drawn as a double or dashed-double wire, never as a repeating pulse.
constructs.quote: A data tree is an ordered collection of lists

constructs.mark: The offending capsule's whole body is repainted orange for a warning or red for an error, and downstream Panels print <null>. No try node, no error grip.
constructs.quote: GH changes the color of components to red or orange to indicate an error warning

constructs.mark: Nothing is drawn. The solver owns every lifetime: data is destroyed and rebuilt each solution. A coloured Group rectangle behind capsules is a backdrop label, not a scope.
constructs.quote: Because the data gets destroyed so readily, we call it Volatile Data

constructs.mark: A Cluster capsule carrying its own lettered grips; double-clicking opens the sub-definition on its own canvas, where the boundary appears as white arrow-shaped Cluster Input/Output tags.
constructs.quote: like the cluster output attached to “L”

constructs.mark: Fan-out needs no node: several beziers simply leave one output grip. Join is a Merge capsule with grips D1, D2 … into R, or Entwine whose grips are named Branch {0;0}, {0;1}.
constructs.quote: Merge a bunch of data streams

constructs.mark: Nothing draws order. It is read off the wires and off left-to-right position alone; to force order without a data dependency you thread a dummy wire or insert a Data Dam.
constructs.quote: It can parse network topology to figure out dependency relationships.

constructs.mark: No receiver arrow and no in-place write anywhere. Every capsule publishes fresh data on its output grip; Rhino geometry is only read in by reference until an explicit Bake.
constructs.quote: Data can be referenced from Rhino or some external document.

constructs.mark: For formulas only: the Evaluate capsule's top grip F is typed Expression, so a formula arrives on a wire from a Panel and is applied to grips x, y.
constructs.quote: Evaluate an expression with a flexible number of variables.

constructs.mark: Undrawable: the board is acyclic, a capsule cannot be wired back into itself, and a Cluster cannot contain a copy of itself. Recursion lives inside a script capsule's text.
There is no name to shadow. A value is only ever the wire into a grip; re-dragging that grip swaps the source in place and nothing records the old one.
constructs.quote: It will manage and synch the source and recipient lists.

constructs.mark: A Deconstruct capsule: one grip P on the left, a stacked column of separately lettered output grips X, Y, Z on the right. Explode Tree fans a tree into Branch 0, Branch 1 grips.
constructs.quote: Deconstruct a point into its component parts.

constructs.mark: Nothing. The whole document re-solves synchronously, so no await mark and no pending state on a grip; a Timer capsule only re-triggers the same solution.
constructs.quote: The user forces a complete solution recalculation (F5).

constructs.mark: Matching mode, Graft, Flatten and Reparameterize are grip settings, not nodes — visible only as tiny StateTag icons stuck to a grip. Wire order into a grip is invisible too.
constructs.quote: It will provide the correct StateTags for DataMapping settings.

identity.flow: left-to-right in the current editor (pins on the left and right walls); the published docs and most screenshots still show an older top-to-bottom build
identity.node_shape: A 160px rounded rectangle (200px 'wide' variant): grey header bar carrying the display name, body below holding one centred FontAwesome icon
identity.port_style: Named text labels inside each wall, inputs left and outputs right, each with an 8px white half-disc handle straddling the border. No types
identity.wire_style: Grey 2.5px bezier, curvature 0.3, source-right to target-left; brand blue when selected, green #4bac00 while a value passes at runtime
identity.one_line: Every node is the same header-and-body card and the only wire is a grey data bezier, so branching, looping, ordering and error handling are all drawn as extra NAMED PINS on that one card rather than as a second wire or an enclosing region.

constructs.mark: A 160px rounded card: grey header bar with the node's name, body below with a centred icon; input labels line the left wall, outputs the right.
constructs.named_thing: Node (Code Node / Visual Node / Macro Node)
constructs.quote: Each node in Flyde is an isolated, modular unit that runs some logic when it is executed.

constructs.mark: A bare text label hugging the wall, inputs left and outputs right, each with an 8px white half-disc handle straddling the border. Names only, no type colour.
constructs.quote: A node has inputs and outputs that allow it to interact with other nodes.

constructs.mark: Dragging a node out of the library drops another identical card; two uses are two cards with separate ids. No arrow ever points back to the definition.
constructs.quote: every Flow is also a visual node, this means you can import and use other flows as nodes

constructs.mark: Nothing is drawn. A value has no name, it IS the grey bezier, labelled only by the pin it lands on. Set State keys a global store instead.
constructs.quote: Gets a value from the global state

constructs.mark: A small card whose header IS the literal, a pencil icon beside "Hello," or 1, one 'value' output on the right wall and a bolt trigger pin on the left.
constructs.quote: This is Flyde's version of a constant. It emits a single value to its output.

constructs.mark: An ordinary card with no special shape: '+ Add', 'x Multiply' with n1/n2 on the left and sum on the right. The operator glyph is just the node icon.
constructs.quote: Emits the sum of two numbers

constructs.mark: One card, circle-question icon, header reading the predicate in words ('Equals "Some value"'), and two output pins on the right wall named true and false. Exactly one fires.
constructs.named_thing: Conditional (n-way: Switch, one pin per case plus 'default')
constructs.quote: Evaluates the condition, and if it's true, emits the left operand value to the 'true' output

constructs.mark: No ternary node. Both true and false outputs carry the same value, so you re-join them onto one input pin; or a Switch case's outputExpression computes what it emits.
constructs.quote: Allows you to switch between multiple outputs based on the value of one input or more

constructs.mark: A plain card, list in on the left, item/index/length out on the right. 'item' fires once per element, so the loop body is simply whatever is wired downstream.
constructs.named_thing: Loop List (aliases: each, spread); also Repeat
constructs.quote: Will emit a value for each item in the list

constructs.mark: No while region and no back-edge marker. You wire a Conditional's output back into an upstream input, an ordinary grey bezier curving backwards, or loop inside a code node.
No break, continue or return glyph. A node that should stop simply emits nothing on that output, or raises, surfacing on the error pin instead of a control mark.
constructs.quote: Item will be emitted until the limit is reached

constructs.mark: No accumulator ring and no state pin. Feedback is an ordinary bezier curving backwards; Collect and Accumulate hide the carried value in a code-side state map.
constructs.named_thing: Collect / Accumulate Some Values by Count
constructs.quote: Collects values into a list. Over time, count, or trigger.

constructs.mark: No map or filter node exists in the standard library. You draw three cards, Loop List then a transform then Collect, or put .map() inside one Code Expression card.
No pin shape marks it; any output may fire repeatedly. Only runtime shows it: the wire flashes green and the pin tooltip reads 'Activated N times this session'.
constructs.quote: nodes can have multiple outputs, and can emit values to their outputs multiple times

constructs.mark: A special output pin labelled 'error' on the right wall, hidden until right-click then 'Show output Error'. Left unwired the failure bubbles up to the parent flow.
constructs.quote: To "catch" an error and avoid it from propagating, you can expose the "Error" special output.

constructs.mark: Nothing. No 'with' frame, no scope box, no lifetime bracket; cleanup lives in a code node's onCleanup callback and leaves no mark whatsoever on the canvas.
constructs.quote: Subscribes to a value published by a key. Use 'Publish' to publish values.

constructs.mark: Right-click 'Group selected instances' collapses cards into one ordinary card. Double-click opens a full-screen modal titled 'Editing inline node ...' holding a nested canvas, never an in-place zoom.
constructs.named_thing: Visual Node / inline node; 'Ungroup inline node'
constructs.quote: a group of nodes that are grouped together visually, and can be reused as a single node

constructs.mark: Many beziers leave one output pin, with no splitter and no junction dot. They re-join by landing on the same input pin, which queues them and shows 'N in Q'.
constructs.quote: Whenever a node emits a value to one of its outputs, the value is sent to all the inputs

constructs.mark: A lightning-bolt glyph replaces the text label on a left-wall 'trigger' pin, revealed by right-click 'Show trigger input'. Wire anything into it to force order without data.
constructs.quote: you may expose a "Trigger" input, which will act as a manual trigger for the node

constructs.mark: Nothing distinguishes it. Set Property and Set State are ordinary cards taking the object in on the left and emitting out the right, so it reads as plain dataflow.
constructs.quote: Used to retrieve a property from an object.

constructs.mark: No function-shaped pin and no socket that accepts a node. Pins carry emitted values only; higher-order behaviour becomes routing, or a closure hidden inside a Code Node.
The node's own card placed on its own canvas: two cards titled 'Fibonacci' sit inside the Fibonacci flow, fed by two Equals false outputs. No recursion badge exists.
constructs.quote: Fibonacci sequence in Flyde - a recursive flow example.

constructs.mark: No name exists to shadow. Two wires into one input pin both deliver; which one wins is the pin's Queued/Sticky mode, chosen in a right-click menu and drawn nowhere.
constructs.quote: The input will keep its last value throughout it's parent node/flow's lifecycle.

constructs.mark: One 'list' input on the left and N output pins named item1..itemN on the right, N set 1-7 by a Count field. For records, one Get Property card per field.
constructs.quote: Receives an array and emits its values as separate outputs

constructs.mark: Invisible on the card. A promise-returning node just stays in Running; the only cue is at runtime, where the wire holds green while the value is still in flight.
constructs.quote: the node will implicitly complete when the promise resolves

constructs.mark: A code node's body: the card shows only a header, an icon and pin names, and right-click 'View/fork code' jumps to the TypeScript. Types and input modes are undrawn too.
constructs.named_thing: Code Node run function; View/fork code
constructs.quote: Its logic, which is the code that runs when the node is executed.

identity.node_shape: A rounded rectangle, pastel fill by palette category, small icon panel on the left behind a vertical rule, italic name label.
identity.port_style: Grey rounded-square nubs straddling the node edge: at most one input left, outputs stacked right. Positional and untyped; name only on hover.
identity.wire_style: A thick grey bezier curve, always the same colour, carrying a whole msg object. Dashed only for splices and link nodes' virtual wires.
identity.one_line: One uniform grey wire carries a whole msg object left-to-right between pastel rounded rectangles; control flow is which output nub the message leaves by, never a second kind of wire.

constructs.mark: Rounded rect, thick orange outline, hierarchy icon, italic name; one grey input nub left, output nubs right. A palette entry you instantiate, not a canvas region.
constructs.quote: A subflow is a collection of nodes that are collapsed into a single node in the workspace.

constructs.mark: Small grey rounded-square nubs straddling the node's left and right edges; at most one left, outputs stacked down the right. Order is identity; names only on hover.
constructs.quote: A node can have at most one input port and many output ports.

constructs.mark: Small square node, orange ring, arrow-into-chevron glyph. Its wire to the callee is dashed grey and drawn only while the link node is selected.
constructs.named_thing: link call / link in / link return
constructs.quote: Calls a flow that starts with a link in node and passes on the response.

constructs.mark: Nothing on the wire. A pale-yellow Change node's dialog rows read Set msg.payload to …; the name is text inside the node, invisible on canvas.
constructs.quote: Set a property to a value,

constructs.mark: Pale blue-grey Inject node: right-arrow icon, no input nub, a click button on its left edge. Otherwise a typed literal row inside a Change dialog.
constructs.quote: That value can either be a hardcoded value, such as a string or number

constructs.mark: No operator glyph. a+b is typed as JSONata in a Change node's to field, or JavaScript in an orange Function node — text in a dialog, never a shape.
constructs.quote: It also supports using the JSONata expression language to calculate a new value.

constructs.mark: Pale-yellow #E2D96E node, crossing-arrows icon; one input nub left, one output nub per rule stacked down the right edge, matching rule text shown on hover.
constructs.quote: A node may specify labels, for example, the Switch node shows the rule that matches the port.

constructs.mark: Not drawn. Author types a JSONata ternary into a Change node's to field, or fans a Switch to two wires that a later node re-merges.
constructs.quote: An Otherwise rule can be used to match if none of the preceeding rules have matched.

constructs.mark: Three pale-yellow nodes in a left-to-right row — split icon, body, join icon — joined by ordinary grey wires. No enclosure, no back edge, no visible count.
constructs.quote: the Split node can turn a single message whose payload is an Array, into a message sequence

constructs.mark: No while enclosure. A grey wire bends back leftwards from a downstream Switch output into an earlier node, usually via a Delay; the guard hides inside the Switch.
constructs.quote: There is no core while enclosure.

constructs.mark: Nothing drawn. The Function returns null, or a Change node sets msg.reset; the wire stays on the canvas and simply never lights up.
constructs.quote: If the function returns null, then no message is passed on and the flow ends.

constructs.mark: Invisible. No node, port or wire shows context; a counter is flow.get/flow.set text inside a Function node. Only a bent-back grey wire hints at it.
constructs.quote: The following example maintains a count of how many times the function has been run

constructs.mark: One pale-yellow node, no loop drawn: a Join set to reduce sequence, or a Change node whose to row holds a JSONata $map/$filter expression.
constructs.quote: allows a JSONata expression to be run against each message in the sequence and the result accumulated

constructs.mark: No mark — every output nub may fire any number of times. A sequence shows only as the Split node's fork icon and msg.parts in the Debug sidebar.
constructs.quote: A message sequence is an ordered series of messages that are related in some way.

constructs.mark: Dusty-red #e49191 node, white exclamation icon, labelled catch: all. It has NO input nub, so no wire reaches it; it sits on a detached row below.
constructs.quote: there is no direct visual association between a Catch node and the nodes it targets

constructs.mark: Drawn nowhere. A shared connection is a Configuration node living only in a sidebar list and a dropdown; cleanup is node.on('close') text.
constructs.quote: as a config node has no icon or ports to set labels on

constructs.mark: Collapsed: one orange-ringed rounded rect. Drilled into: a new workspace tab whose interface is grey square input/output nodes you wire to like any other node.
constructs.quote: The inputs and outputs of the subflow are represented by the grey square nodes

constructs.mark: Fan-out: several grey wires leaving one output nub. Convergence on an input nub only interleaves — a real join is a separate stateful pale-yellow Join node.
constructs.quote: Turns a sequence of messages into a single message.

constructs.mark: No order-only edge exists. The single grey wire kind always carries the msg, so the author chains nodes in series and lets the message act as the token.
constructs.quote: A wire carries messages from one output port to an input port.

constructs.mark: Pale-yellow node, swap-arrows icon; dialog lists Set/Change/Delete/Move rows. msg is mutated in place, so the outgoing wire looks identical to the incoming one.
constructs.quote: There are two main nodes for modifying a message, the Function node and the Change

constructs.mark: No callable port or wire type. Nearest is a link call set to Dynamic target, where the callee's NAME rides as a string in msg.target — undrawn.
constructs.quote: msg.target can be used to call a link in by name or id

constructs.mark: Not drawable: a subflow may not contain itself. Instead a grey wire bends back to an earlier node, or a link call re-enters the same flow's link in.
constructs.quote: a subflow cannot contain an instance of itself - either directly or indirectly

constructs.mark: Nothing shadows anything. A second Change node downstream sets msg.payload again; the grey curve before and after is identical, so the overwrite is invisible until a Debug node.
constructs.quote: A common task in a flow is to modify the properties of a message

constructs.mark: Pale-yellow Split node fans a record over TIME on ONE output nub, one message per key — never into several named ports. Field names ride in msg.parts.key.
constructs.quote: a message is sent for each key/value pair of the object

constructs.mark: No await mark — every wire is already asynchronous delivery. Long work is node.send()/node.done() text in a Function, or a Delay node; concurrency is never drawn.
constructs.quote: it must make use of the node.send() function, passing in the message(s) to be sent

constructs.mark: Everything behind a node's edit dialog: rules, JSONata, JavaScript, context keys, config nodes. Catch's target list too — which is why it sits wireless on its own row.
constructs.quote: Another approach is to group all of the error handling flows below the main flow

identity.node_shape: A white rounded-square tile with the app icon centred, bold node name beneath it, grey operation subtitle, and a green check badge after a run.
identity.port_style: Grey bar on the left wall is input, grey dot on the right is output; extras labelled true/false or Input 1/Input 2.
identity.wire_style: A thin curved bezier left-to-right carrying an item-count label; green once data flowed through it, pale grey when none did.
identity.one_line: One wire kind carrying an array of items left to right, every node looping over them invisibly, and canvas position deciding what runs first.

constructs.mark: A white rounded-square tile, icon centred, bold name below, grey operation subtitle. Tiles are built-ins you configure; a user-defined reusable unit is a whole separate workflow.
constructs.quote: A node is an entry point for retrieving data, a function to process data, or an exit

constructs.mark: Input is a small grey vertical bar with an arrowhead on the left wall; output is a grey filled dot on the right wall. Positional, untyped.
constructs.quote: on the right side of a node and slide the arrow to the grey rectangle on the left side

constructs.mark: An ordinary tile named Execute Sub-workflow. The callee is not drawn here at all: it is another workflow, picked from a dropdown, opened in its own tab.
constructs.quote: Use the Execute Sub-workflow node to run a different workflow on the host machine that runs n8n.

constructs.mark: A purple pencil-in-square Edit Fields tile. The names are rows in its side panel only; the wire leaving it carries no name, just an item count.
constructs.quote: Use the Edit Fields node to set workflow data.

constructs.mark: A value typed into a parameter field with its Fixed | Expressions toggle set to Fixed. Lives inside the node panel; nothing appears on the canvas.
constructs.quote: Hover over a field. n8n displays the Fixed | Expressions toggle.

constructs.mark: A {{ }} expression typed into a field after flipping it to Expression mode, with a live result preview under it. No node, no wire, no shape.
constructs.quote: switch the field to expression mode, then drag a value from the INPUT pane into it

constructs.mark: Signpost-icon If tile with two stacked grey dots on its right wall, tiny lowercase true above false printed outside the tile. Switch stacks one dot per rule.
constructs.named_thing: If node (true / false outputs); Switch node (Routing Rules, Fallback Output)
constructs.quote: Use the If node to split a workflow conditionally based on comparison operations.

constructs.mark: No mark. The author types a JavaScript ternary inside {{ }} in one parameter field, or splits with If and rejoins with Merge. The choice is never a shape.
constructs.quote: You can use expression transformation functions anywhere expressions are supported in n8n.
